short_answer: On a normal day the air in January was cleaner than in December: a typical day had 9.48 instead of 12.66 micrograms of fine dust per cubic metre. But the average over all days was higher in January: 18.01 against 16.42.
what_it_means: Most January days were cleaner, but a few very polluted days pulled the January average up. The official background station nearby also measured more in January (15.31 against 13.84), which points to pollution over the whole region rather than a source in your own street.
how_sure: We used 48 of the 54 sensors within 2 km: 5 were left out because they were broken, and some had too little data. On 26.65% of the hours the air was very damp, and these sensors then tend to read too high. Both the typical day and the average are correct; they answer slightly different questions.
how_we_got_this: Sensors within 2 km of central Beverwijk, December 2024 and January 2025, calibrated PM2.5
Broken sensors and impossible values removed first; damp hours flagged
Daily value per sensor, then the area's typical day (median) and average (mean)
Compared with the nearest official background station (Luchtmeetnet)
